newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slide on land buying report.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slide on land buying report.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures subsided in line with a steep drop in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Thursday following hefty gains on the Nikkei.

Dealers said most of the activity was driven by a Japanese newspaper report that said the government may use public funds to buy land formerly owned by failed housing loan companies and other troubled financial firms.
The market was unaffected by news of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's death overnight.
March JGBs fell to a low of 125.50 on the back of the land buying report. They recovered some ground to close at 125.68 against a previous 126.62 on above average volume of 2,270 lots.
A trader with a U.S. house said some stop-loss sell orders were triggered at around 125.80.

But he said the market recovered marginally on a later report quoting a Japanese Finance Ministry official as saying the government was not considering allocating new public funds to buy collateralised land now held by loan-collecting bodies.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.35 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.38 on volume of 16,000 lots. December was at 99.23 against 99.27 on 11,590 lots.

Dealers said vague rumours that the Wall Street Journal was going to run a story saying the United States and Japan might jointly hike interest rates also kept pressure on the market although few participants attached much credence to it.
"I think they may do it but not so soon. So there's no panic on that for the time being," said the trader.
Eurodollar futures remained sluggish despite the rate hike talk with September ending at 94.27 against its opening 94.28 and its IMM close at 94.29. Turnover was 7,895 lots.
"Eurodollars came off maybe a tick or two but it was nothing much. I don't think people would believe it (the report) anyway," said a dealer at a European institution.
